WoW: Forever

Retribution Paladin

Two-handed melee with Holy magic layered on top. Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage. at level 6 turns it from auto-attack-and-wait into something you actually play, twenty levels earlier than Classic gave a Paladin a button.

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 16, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70374 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30, so no level-60 Retribution build has been tested. Blizzard published its Paladin class deep dive on October 15, the last of the series, and this page is written from it and then read back against the client at build 1.60.1.70374. Where Blizzard speaks, Blizzard is the source; where it says nothing, the client is, and figures that are only a guide site's are marked.

Talents open at 10. Blizzard keeps the one-point gold medal talents at 11, 21 and 31 points and has added a new one at 16 points, which for Retribution is Sacred ArbiterSacred ArbiterTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage of your Holy Strike ability by 20% and causes it to refresh all Judgement effects on the target. at around level 25. RepentanceRepentanceTalentCastInstantCost60 ManaRange20 yd rangeCooldown60 sec cooldownDuration6 secPuts the enemy target in a state of meditation, incapacitating them for up to 6 sec. Any damage caused will awaken the target. Only works against Humanoids. sits at 21 points now and Twist of LightTwist of LightSpell · PhysicalCastInstantReduces the Mana cost of your Seal spells by 20%, and when you replace your Seal of Command, Seal of Righteousness, Seal of Fury, or Seal of Justice with a different Seal, you gain an Echo of that Seal. Your next melee attack applies the replaced Seal's effects, consuming the Echo. at 31. Dual Specialization opens at 40. Blizzard's own caveat: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

CrusadeCrusadeTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage dealt by 2%. Increased by an additional 2% against Demon and Undead targets. is almost certainly still spendable. A widely-published level-30 build puts two points in it, and Blizzard's removal list for this tree names only Improved Retribution AuraImproved Retribution AuraTalent · Rank 1 of 2CastInstantIncreases the damage done by your Retribution Aura by 25%. and Sanctity AuraSanctity AuraTalentCastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases Holy damage done by party members within 30 yards by 10%. Players may only have one Aura on them per Paladin at any one time.. The client carries CrusadeCrusadeTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage dealt by 2%. Increased by an additional 2% against Demon and Undead targets. with working text: 2% to all damage, and 2% more against Demons and Undead. Neither of those proves the tree can reach it, because the client keeps a record after a talent leaves a tree, so confirm it in game before you commit the points. Improved Holy StrikeImproved Holy StrikeTalentCastInstantReduces the cooldown of your Holy Strike ability by 2 sec. is in exactly the same position.

Champion of the LightChampion of the LightTalentCastInstantIncreases your spell damage by up to 100% of your Intellect. converts up to 30% of your Intellect into spell damage. That is Blizzard's own talent line, so that is the figure this page publishes, while the same article's designer note describes a cut to 60% and the client still reads 100% — the magnitude is still moving, so build for the direction rather than the number.

Three kinds of caveat run through these pages and they do not mean the same thing. Something marked as ours is our own reasoning rather than a source's. A client or a guide-site reading is a number Blizzard has not published. The third case is Blizzard having published something the game does not have yet: on this page that is Improved Seal of the CrusaderImproved Seal of the CrusaderTalent · Rank 1 of 3CastInstantIncreases the melee attack power bonus of your Seal of the Crusader and the Holy damage increase of your Judgement of the Crusader by 5%., where Blizzard says the Judgement bonus is baseline now and the client's talent still grants it.

The hover tooltips on this page come from the client index at build 1.60.1.70374 — the same build this page was checked against — not from Blizzard's article. Where a tooltip and the prose disagree, believe the prose: it is Blizzard's figure, and the tooltip is the number the game is showing.

Wowhead reports that beta testers and class discords consider Retribution the single most overtuned spec in the level-20 bracket, and expects changes. Treat the talent and gearing advice below as a snapshot.

What Retribution is for

Layering Holy damage onto a two-handed swing, with a real button to press from level 6. Seal of CommandSeal of CommandLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost65 ManaDuration30 secGives the Paladin a chance to deal additional Holy damage equal to 70% of normal weapon damage. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Lasts 30 sec. Unleashing this Seal's energy will judge an enemy, instantly causing 48.5 Holy damage, 97 if the target is stunned or incapacitated. at 20 procs Holy damage scaled off the swing, and a stun amplifies its Judgement.

Blizzard's framing for the spec is three things: new ways to sustain Judgements, weapon attacks blended with Holy damage, and a more approachable form of Seal Twisting. Sustaining Judgements starts in row 3 with Sanctified JudgementSanctified JudgementTalentCastInstantGives your Judgement ability a 100% chance to return 60% of the Mana cost of the judged seal.. The Seal Twisting arrives only at 31 points, far past the beta's cap.

Wowhead's overtuning warning is the only published comment aimed squarely at this spec. It is not a levelling score: no source publishes one for any Paladin spec, and a score would only measure solo kill speed.

You have no area damage until ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. at 20. Blizzard trains it to every Paladin now instead of selling it as a Holy talent, and it only damages four enemies properly. Pull one target at a time.

Blizzard states the class has no interrupt and no way to slow an enemy's movement, and that Holy talents widen its range without matching other mana users. Your own speed comes from one talent, Pursuit of JusticePursuit of JusticeTalentCastInstantIncreases movement speed and mounted movement speed by 15%. This does not stack with other movement speed increasing effects.. The published guides still call the class "slow, very slow."

Treat mana as an extension of your health bar. Topping up with Holy LightHoly LightLevel 1 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 9Cast2.5 sec castCost35 ManaRange40 yd rangeHeals a friendly target for 43. and killing the next thing at low mana usually beats sitting down to drink.

A level-20 or level-30 build labelled for twisting is a build for the weapon and the seal choice, not for the twist.

Multi-target: none until 20. Then ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec., and it is expensive: 135 Mana at rank 1, on an 8-second cooldown. Blizzard limits what it can do on purpose: moderate damage to the first 4 enemies that walk into it, very low damage to everything after that, so Paladin threat stays level with a Warrior's Thunderclap. The thin damage on the fifth target is the design, and Blizzard says the limit keeps Forever out of expansion-era AoE pulling. The client agrees. Its rank 1 does 16 Holy damage over 8 seconds to anything in the area, with an extra 32 over 8 seconds for the first four. A separate beta fix repaired the spell failing to apply that bonus to some targets, along with its inconsistent Z axis.

Later, Sacred ArbiterSacred ArbiterTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage of your Holy Strike ability by 20% and causes it to refresh all Judgement effects on the target. gives Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage. +20% damage and makes it refresh every Judgement effect on the target, even those from other Paladins, so staying in melee maintains them without re-judging. Blizzard puts it at the new 16-point gold medal, around level 25; the client's thinner text stops at the Judgements on the target without naming whose they are.

Stat priority

Weapon DPS, then Hit and Expertise, critical strike, Spell Power, Strength, Intellect, Agility, Stamina.

Hit and Expertise barely appear on gear at this level, so they are close to irrelevant below 30. A slower weapon makes Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage. hit harder, but raw weapon DPS usually wins.

Intellect matters much more from 26 points in the tree, at level 35, where Champion of the LightChampion of the LightTalentCastInstantIncreases your spell damage by up to 100% of your Intellect. starts converting it into spell damage. Blizzard places the talent in row 6 of this tree.

It converts up to 30% of your Intellect, which is Blizzard's talent line and the figure to build against. The designers' note in the same article describes a cut to 60% partway through the beta, and the client at 1.60.1.70374 still reads 100%, so the magnitude has not finished moving — but the direction is agreed on every reading: Intellect becomes a damage stat for a Retribution Paladin who goes that deep. Wowhead, Icy Veins and ClassicWoW.gg may print any of the three figures.

Blizzard confines the effect to damage. A tooltip line that claimed the talent raised Healing is gone, and it never did raise Healing, so read it as spell damage only.

Published gear lists split into a Spell Power build and an Attack Power build, and call both competitive at level 20.

At level 60

Unknown, and Blizzard frames it as a choice rather than a puzzle. Retribution can twist seals with Twist of LightTwist of LightSpell · PhysicalCastInstantReduces the Mana cost of your Seal spells by 20%, and when you replace your Seal of Command, Seal of Righteousness, Seal of Fury, or Seal of Justice with a different Seal, you gain an Echo of that Seal. Your next melee attack applies the replaced Seal's effects, consuming the Echo. or hybridise into Holy ShockHoly ShockLevel 30 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 4CastInstantCost160 ManaRange40 yd rangeCooldown10 sec cooldownBlasts the target with Holy energy, causing 134 Holy damage to an enemy, or 114 healing to an ally. for Holy damage, and Blizzard positioned Holy ShockHoly ShockLevel 30 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 4CastInstantCost160 ManaRange40 yd rangeCooldown10 sec cooldownBlasts the target with Holy energy, causing 134 Holy damage to an enemy, or 114 healing to an ally. as the alternative so that opting out of twisting is a real build. Neither side has been tested at 51 points. The author of one published guide says "it's looking like twisting might not be the way to go for Paladin raid DPS specs atm." Blizzard's closing line is that Retribution stays a strong damage dealer with steadier damage and more group utility, naming Sacred ArbiterSacred ArbiterTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage of your Holy Strike ability by 20% and causes it to refresh all Judgement effects on the target. and its upkeep of other Paladins' Judgements as the example.
